From 85d98669fa7f1d3041d962515e45ee6e392db6f8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Loic Poulain <loic.poulain@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:26:03 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: qcom: monaco: Reserve full Gunyah metadata region
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

We observe spurious "Synchronous External Abort" exceptions
(ESR=0x96000010) and kernel crashes on Monaco-based platforms.
These faults are caused by the kernel inadvertently accessing
hypervisor-owned memory that is not properly marked as reserved.

>From boot log, The Qualcomm hypervisor reports the memory range
at 0x91a80000 of size 0x80000 (512 KiB) as hypervisor-owned:
qhee_hyp_assign_remove_memory: 0x91a80000/0x80000 -> ret 0

However, the EFI memory map provided by firmware only reserves the
subrange 0x91a40000–0x91a87fff (288 KiB). The remaining portion
(0x91a88000–0x91afffff) is incorrectly reported as conventional
memory (from efi debug):
efi:   0x000091a40000-0x000091a87fff [Reserved...]
efi:   0x000091a88000-0x0000938fffff [Conventional...]

As a result, the allocator may hand out PFNs inside the hypervisor
owned region, causing fatal aborts when the kernel accesses those
addresses.

Add a reserved-memory carveout for the Gunyah hypervisor metadata
at 0x91a80000 (512 KiB) and mark it as no-map so Linux does not
map or allocate from this area.

For the record:
Hyp version: gunyah-e78adb36e debug (2025-11-17 05:38:05 UTC)
UEFI Ver: 6.0.260122.BOOT.MXF.1.0.c1-00449-KODIAKLA-1

Fixes: 7be190e4bdd2 ("arm64: dts: qcom: add QCS8300 platform")
Signed-off-by: Loic Poulain <loic.poulain@oss.qualcomm.com>
Reviewed-by: Konrad Dybcio <konrad.dybcio@oss.qualcomm.com>
Reviewed-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260302142603.1113355-1-loic.poulain@oss.qualcomm.com
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <andersson@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/monaco.dtsi b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/monaco.dtsi
index dbb2273b0ee8..0cb9fd154b68 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/monaco.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/monaco.dtsi
@@ -765,6 +765,11 @@ smem_mem: smem@90900000 {
 			hwlocks = <&tcsr_mutex 3>;
 		};
 
+		gunyah_md_mem: gunyah-md-region@91a80000 {
+			reg = <0x0 0x91a80000 0x0 0x80000>;
+			no-map;
+		};
+
 		lpass_machine_learning_mem: lpass-machine-learning-region@93b00000 {
 			reg = <0x0 0x93b00000 0x0 0xf00000>;
 			no-map;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Files Modified

- **arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/monaco.dtsi**:  
  Added a new `reserved-memory` child node `gunyah_md_mem` within the `/reserved-memory` section. The node specifies:
  - `reg = <0x0 0x91a80000 0x0 0x80000>` (physical base 0x91a80000, size 512 KiB)
  - `no-map` property to prevent the kernel from creating a page table mapping for this region.

### Relationships Between Changes

The single-file modification is a targeted fix for a memory region misalignment problem on the Monaco platform. The field-reported symptom (Synchronous External Abort, ESR=0x96000010) was traced to the kernel allocating and accessing pages that belong to the Gunyah hypervisor’s metadata area. Although the hypervisor correctly claimed the full 0x91a80000–0x91afffff range, the firmware’s EFI memory map only reserved a sub-range (0x91a40000–0x91a87fff), leaving the rest marked as conventional memory. This inconsistency allowed the Linux page allocator to hand out PFNs inside the hypervisor-owned region.

By explicitly carving out the entire hypervisor metadata region (matching the hypervisor-assigned area) and marking it as `no-map`, the patch ensures:
- Linux will never map or allocate from this region.
- The memory is fully protected from inadvertent access, eliminating the external abort crashes.
- The device tree override corrects the firmware’s incomplete reservation without requiring firmware updates.

Here is the root cause:
The firmware's EFI memory map incorrectly reports a portion of the hypervisor-owned Gunyah metadata region (0x91a88000–0x91afffff) as conventional memory, while the actual hypervisor-owned range is 0x91a80000–0x91afffff (512 KiB). This mismatch allows the Linux kernel's page allocator to hand out PFNs inside the hypervisor-owned region, causing Synchronous External Abort exceptions when the kernel accesses those addresses. The missing device tree reservation for the full hypervisor metadata region exacerbated the issue.
